claim: The mist absorbs about 18.8 kW from the air while spraying
law: Q = m_dot x 0.87 evaporated x latent heat (2.43 MJ/kg) for 8 nozzles x 4 L/h = 18.8 kW; the 0.87 evaporated share is an estimate that falls as the droplets get bigger (S4), and drops that drift out of the zone (CSH-CAL-001 D2) cool air outside it, so the share that cools the waiting zone is a range, not a point
check: Arithmetic checks out (independent review); the evaporated share inside the zone needs the nozzle's droplet spectrum

claim: The air in the waiting zone is at least 2 degC cooler while spraying (2.71 degC computed)
law: Sensible heat removed from a 3 x 2 m control volume crossed by air at 1 m/s: dT = Q / (m_dot cp); assumes the mist mixes through the whole volume, which real spray plumes do not (CSH-PRS-001 assumptions); the control volume's 3 m is used both as the frontal width and as the transit length, so the drop moves by about 25 % with the wind direction
check: 2.71 degC >= 2 degC

claim: Misting cannot cool the air below the wet bulb (design day: 15 degC below ambient)
law: Adiabatic saturation limit: dry-bulb depression is at most T_air - T_wetbulb (Stull wet bulb, 38 degC at 25 % RH)
check: 2.71 degC <= 15 degC

claim: Droplets from the nozzle evaporate before they reach a person at 1.5 m (no wetting)
law: Droplet evaporation after Maxwell/Fuchs diffusion: on the design day a droplet of up to about 100 um evaporates in the 0.76 m between the jet end and head height, at the humid edge (32 degC, 60 %) up to about 80 um (CSH-CAL-001 D3); nozzle makers state the spectrum as Dv0.9
check: Needs Dv0.9 below about 80 um at 7 bar; no maker's data yet. At risk: fog that flash-evaporates is normally made at much higher pressure (50 bar and more), and a 7 bar spectrum is likely coarser; if it is, wetting (PR-005) and cooling (S1, S2) fail together and option B becomes the fallback

claim: Each 0.4 mm nozzle can pass 4 L/h at 7 bar (the physical bound is 16.9 L/h; the real flow is the maker's figure)
law: A bound only, not a prediction: Bernoulli orifice flow Q = A sqrt(2 dp / rho): ideal 16.9 L/h, so 4 L/h implies a discharge coefficient of 0.24, plausible for a swirl nozzle (maker's datasheet to confirm)

claim: The 60 W pump draw covers the hydraulic power of 32 L/h at 7 bar
law: Hydraulic power = Q x dp; the rest is motor and diaphragm loss (10 % wire to water)
check: in 60 W, out 6.222 W

claim: The bulk of the mist line drains within 5 min after a session (about 30 s computed); water films and the anti-drip nozzle bodies stay wet
law: Torricelli flow through the 3 mm valve orifice at 0.5 m head (Cd 0.6), with air let in by the vacuum breaker; the 0.40 L line volume from the model

claim: A 100 W panel of 1.0 x 0.67 m is a credible rating
law: Efficiency = P / (1000 W/m2 x area) must stay below the Shockley-Queisser limit for a single junction (33.7 %); commercial monocrystalline panels reach about 20 %

claim: The panel harvests more energy per design day than the system uses
law: Conservation of energy, with 0.75 for MPPT, wiring and temperature losses; holds on the design day only: on days above 42.7 degC charging pauses at midday (S11)
check: in 337.5 Wh, out 203.8 Wh

claim: The battery runs the system for a full design day with no sun
law: Usable energy = 12.8 V x 25 Ah x 0.80 depth of discharge divided by the daily use, at beginning of life (at 80 % state of health it is about 1.0 design days, and cells at 40 to 47 degC age faster)
check: 1.26 design days >= 1 design days

claim: The battery keeps charging on hot days: LiFePO4 charge limit 45 degC against an enclosure 2.3 K above the air (white enclosure, in the cloth's shade)
law: Enclosure heat balance dT = (alpha G A_face + Q_internal) / (h A), G = 200 W/m2 in the shade of the cloth; cells are charged only below about 45 degC (typical cell data; the BMS reads cell temperature, which runs above the air in the box). The original grey enclosure (alpha 0.5) rose 3.6 K and stopped charging above 41.4 degC air; the white one (CSH-DEC-001 D9) rises 2.3 K, charging holds to 42.7 degC air. In direct late sun (900 W/m2, the enclosure is on the outer face of the rear right post) the white enclosure rises 7.0 K and charging stops above 38.0 degC air, so the fix is partial
check: Sun exposure of the enclosure across the day, long-wave exchange with the hot slab and the named cell's charge limit to assess at the site; a sunshield on the enclosure is a candidate

claim: Scale from hard water does not block the 0.4 mm nozzles within a month
law: Calcium carbonate precipitates as the mist evaporates and when water warms; orifices of 0.4 mm clog from a few mg of deposit; a 5 um filter does not remove dissolved hardness
check: Hardness of the site water and descaling interval to assess at the site (CSH-DEC-001 to-confirm item 12)

claim: Shade cuts the mean radiant temperature by at least 15 degC at midday
law: Measured in Tempe, Arizona at 159 locations: shade sails and umbrellas cut the daytime mean radiant temperature by about 17.3 degC (Middel et al., BAMS 2021)
check: Evidence from analogous shade sails, not this design: 17.3 degC measured against the 15 degC target, a margin of 2.3 K on a site average; this cloth (about 90 % UV block, which is not 90 % of the shortwave) and the occupied spots, where the shadow falls partly outside the roof footprint at low sun (CSH-CAL-001 A2), are unmeasured; confirm with a globe thermometer

claim: The misting system does not become a Legionella source
law: Legionella grows in water at 20 to 50 degC (optimum about 35 degC) and spreads by inhaled aerosol (WHO fact sheet). Tank water on a design day settles near 34 degC (CSH-CAL-001 I3), inside the growth range; the controls are a 5 um filter, water no older than 24 h (95 L drain-and-refill), the bulk of the line drained within 30 s (films and the anti-drip nozzle bodies stay wet), an opaque shaded tank and weekly disinfection
check: Temperature cannot be avoided; water age and cleaning are the controls; sampling with a partner lab needs TRL 4

claim: A passive infrared sensor detects people standing still in 38 to 45 degC air
law: A PIR sensor responds to the contrast between a warm body (skin about 33 to 35 degC, clothing cooler) and its background; in air near body temperature the contrast and the detection range fall, and a person standing still gives little signal (sensor datasheets derate range with ambient temperature)
check: Range and sensitivity above 35 degC to take from the sensor maker; a radar presence sensor is a privacy and radio-approval trade-off for Amish (CSH-DEC-001 D10)

claim: A front post (80 x 80 x 3 SHS, 2.90 m) weighs about 21 kg
law: Mass = section area x length x 7850 kg/m3
check: claimed 21 kg, estimate 21 kg (ratio 1.00)

claim: With the fabric fitted the long beams carry forecast gusts up to 15 m/s (the original 30 m/s case gives utilization 3.5 and failed; fixed by removing the fabric above 15 m/s, CSH-DDR-002)
law: Fabric as a membrane with 5 % sag: edge pull T = p L^2 / (8 s) per metre, in-plane bending of the 50 x 50 x 2 SHS long beam over the 2.8 m post span, S275 with a 1.5 factor
check: 0.88 utilization <= 1 utilization

claim: With the fabric removed the frame survives a 30 m/s gust
law: Post as a cantilever: panel as a flat plate (1.2 q A) with its tilt component plus drag on the frame and posts, S275 with a 1.5 factor (CSH-CAL-001 G13); roof members and anchors in G13 too; recomputed by the independent reviewer as 0.14
check: 0.14 utilization (post) <= 1 utilization (post)

claim: An empty tank tips in a 30 m/s gust unless strapped; the strap carries the difference (the unstrapped tank failed, strap added in CSH-DDR-003)
law: Overturning 57 N m against restoring 21 N m; strap tension = difference / (0.9 x tank height) = 57 N, 86 N with the 1.5 factor; the strap works for some wind directions only, so the two stop cleats are the second restraint; sliding (163 N of drag against about 40 N of friction) is held by the strap and the cleats; the strap's rating is not yet named
check: 86 N factored against a strap of a few hundred newtons or more; rating and cleat anchors to confirm when parts are bought

claim: The M16 anchors hold in the slab at the site
law: Factored anchor tension about 6.4 kN with the fabric on in a 30 m/s gust and about 2.8 kN with it removed (CSH-CAL-001 G10, G13); the resistance depends on the anchor type and the slab, which are unknown until a site is chosen
check: Anchor design resistance and slab to assess at each site

claim: A garage can build the frame: bolted, no welding, rivet nuts in 2 mm tube
law: Blind rivet nuts are standard in thin-wall tube; the largest pull on one M8 rivet nut is about 0.16 kN factored (CSH-CAL-001 G15); the maker's pull-out rating in a 2 mm wall is not yet checked
check: Rating to confirm from the rivet nut maker's data when parts are bought

claim: Option B: the wet pad delivers air at about 26 degC from 38 degC, 25 % RH air
law: Direct evaporative cooling, T_out = T_db - eps (T_db - T_wb), eps 0.8 for a 90 mm cellulose pad (typical, to confirm from the maker); the outlet cannot be below the wet bulb 23.0 degC
check: 26 degC >= 23 degC

claim: Option B: the fan and pad remove about 1.5 kW and evaporate about 2.2 L/h
law: Q = m_dot cp dT = 1.53 kW at 0.11 m3/s; water = Q / latent heat (a pad also needs bleed-off water against scale, which adds 20 to 50 %)
check: claimed 2.2 L/h, estimate 2.27 L/h (ratio 0.97)

claim: Option B: one 250 mm fan cools a group of 6 to 8 people
law: The cooled stream carries 1.5 kW, 8 % of the 18.8 kW that option A's mist absorbs; an axial jet of 0.11 m3/s mixes with room air within about 1 to 2 m, so it cools one or two people, not a group
check: Throw and mixing to confirm with a jet model or a field test; several fans would change the cost and power

claim: Option C: a white skin 100 mm above the shade cloth lowers the heat load and the gap vents by buoyancy
law: Stack effect in a gap 2.4 m long at 7.1 deg, 10 K warmer than the air: v = sqrt(2 g H dT / T) = 0.43 m/s, an upper bound before friction; white coatings reflect most of the sun (reflectance of the maker's panel to confirm)
check: Added radiant benefit over the shade cloth alone to measure; no air cooling at all (no evaporation)

claim: Option C: the skin cannot be taken off before a gust, so the frame must carry 30 m/s with the roof solid
law: Rigid sheets pass the load to the long beams as pressure, not as fabric edge pull: normal force 4.67 kN, long beams 0.70 utilization (CSH-CAL-001 G6); anchors about 6.4 kN each (G10), the slab to assess
check: Beams within; anchors and slab depend on the site
